expectations.text: Covers all five parts: lead magnet, landing page, thank-you page, sales page, follow-up
expectations.evidence: Sections '## 1. Lead Magnet', '## 2. Landing (Opt-in) Page', '## 3. Thank-You Page', '## 4. Sales Page / Offer', '## 5. Follow-Up Sequence' cover all five parts.

expectations.text: Lead magnet uses a curiosity/pain hook (e.g. 'The # Biggest Mistakes...')
expectations.evidence: Magnet 'The 7-Point Used Furniture Checklist: How to Spot Solid Wood, Bedbugs, and Overpriced Junk in 60 Seconds' is a pain-focused curiosity hook ('Fixes a real fear. Buying used is scary'); early access is called 'the real hook'. No book attribution claimed, so no misattribution; no 'Biggest Mistakes' formula, but the assertion's example is only an e.g.

expectations.text: Includes a thank-you-page offer or self-liquidating offer
expectations.evidence: Thank-you page item 4: 'Immediate offer (tripwire / self-liquidator): "Available right now for VIPs only:" ... "Claim It — $20 Hold Deposit"'; section 6 also does an SLO sanity check (15 sales x ~$80 vs $250 ad spend).

expectations.text: Includes list math (e.g. $1 per name per month) with an estimate
expectations.evidence: Section 6 list math: 300 subs/month, 5% churn, 4% buying, $100 profit -> 'Value per subscriber per month = 4% x $100 profit = $4.00', month-by-month growth table, LTV ≈ $80. Concrete estimate given (does not cite the book's $1/name figure, but the assertion's example is an e.g.).

expectations.text: Includes a follow-up sequence or daily publishing plan
expectations.evidence: 'Welcome / indoctrination (first 7 days)' table (Day 0,1,2,3,5,7), weekly Wed/Thu/Sat broadcast rhythm, and behavioral triggers.
